title: 24.1 A 12b 3GS/s Pipelined ADC with Gated-LMS-Based Piecewise-Linear Nonlinearity Calibration
problem: Pipelined ADCs using open-loop residue amplifiers suffer from large gain errors and severe gain nonlinearity; polynomial-based background calibration incurs significant power and area overhead, especially at high sampling rates (>1GS/s).
motivation: Open-loop amplifiers offer speed and energy advantages over closed-loop designs but require practical calibration; polynomial compensation becomes prohibitively expensive at gigahertz sampling rates.
method: The ADC corrects errors from its amplifiers by continuously learning correction factors in the background (while operating normally) instead of stopping for calibration. It uses an adaptive filter that learns piecewise-linear corrections—breaking the error curve into straight-line segments instead of using complex polynomial formulas—with threshold values that adjust based on observed patterns. A dual-path amplification design further improves settling speed and power efficiency.
key_novelty: Continuously learning piecewise-linear corrections with adaptive thresholds in the background eliminates both polynomial computation and calibration downtime.
contributions: PWL nonlinearity calibration replaces polynomial schemes, reducing computational complexity
Gated LMS filter extraction with adaptive thresholds for background operation
Dual-path amplification for improved settling and power efficiency
12b 3GS/s pipelined ADC achieving 58.8dB SNDR, 32.5mW power, 165dB FoM_S, 15.2fJ/conv-step
limitations: Comparison with state-of-the-art 3GS/s ADCs and temperature/process corner performance not discussed.
primary_theme: High-speed pipelined ADC with background LMS-based piecewise-linear calibration
